builder_plan.scenario: A workflow needs specialist review, but extra agents may add more cost than useful work.
builder_plan.change: Test the proposed division of work against a single-agent implementation.
builder_plan.baseline: One agent with the same tools and an equal total token and time budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted outputs, coordination failures, wall-clock time, and total cost across all agents.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Enabling Privacy-Preserving Natural Language Access to Industrial Smart Meter Data
summary: Replaces manual SQL authoring and cloud-based LLM APIs that violate data privacy constraints with a local, schema-agnostic multi-agent pipeline. Costs increased architectural complexity, latency from agent communication overhead, and higher local inference compute compared to single-agent or direct API calls. Small models may fail at complex reasoning tasks, and the accuracy benefits of full orchestration diminish at frontier scale, risking unnecessary overhead if components are not selectively enabled.
rationale: The +6.1 pp accuracy gain on local hardware justifies the complexity for privacy-constrained deployments, but the need for selective component enabling at scale and unvalidated performance on specific schemas requires workload-specific testing before adoption.

claims.statement: Replaces manual SQL authoring and cloud-based LLM APIs that violate data privacy constraints with a local, schema-agnostic multi-agent pipeline. Costs increased architectural complexity, latency from agent communication overhead, and higher local inference compute compared to single-agent or direct API calls. Small models may fail at complex reasoning tasks, and the accuracy benefits of full orchestration diminish at frontier scale, risking unnecessary overhead if components are not selectively enabled.

Full multi-agent orchestration shows largest accuracy gains on resource-constrained local hardware (+6.1 pp EX-R over strongest single-agent configuration); at frontier scale, individual components retain value but should be enabled selectively.
